page.overview:
Who is Tathagata Buddha?

Siddhartha Gautama was born in the distant past, when Heaven and Earth had yet to seperate, and apprenticed under senior Buddhas. One day, he was swallowed whole by the giant peacock Mahamayuri. Gautama was able to cut himself out of the peacock and wanted to kill it, but the older Buddhas stopped him since it would be like killing his mother.

At the personal request of the Jade Emperor, the Tathagata Buddha was summoned to Heaven to deal with Sun Wukong's rampage. The Buddha promised he’d give Sun Wukong control over Heaven if he was able to jump out of the palm of his hand. Since his hand held the entirety of the universe, Sun Wukong obviously failed. When Sun Wukong fled in shock, the Buddha dropped Five Elements Mountain on him.

400 years later, the Tathagata Buddha noticed the rise of immorality on the Southern Continent and wrote the Tripitaka to redeem them. He tasked the Bodhisattva Guanyin with finding a pilgrim worthy to come to Thunderclap Monastery and collect them.

Sun Wukong, who could travel to Thunderclap Monastery easily, occasionally went there to seek the Buddha's advice, such as when he couldn’t defeat the Single Horned Rhinoceros King, or wanted to identify the Six-Eared Macaque. The Tathagata Buddha became personally involved to subdue his spiritual uncle, the Golden-Winged Great Peng.
